notes.text: Colton Parayko is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. Brandon Carlo has taken his spot beside Philip Broberg.

Logan Mailloux is on injured reserve (hand surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Adam Jiříček has taken his spot beside Philip Broberg. That pair has had 65% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 80:05 together.
Matthew Robertson has not dressed for the last 9 games. Alberts Šmits has taken his spot beside Braden Schneider. That pair has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 147:07 together.
Sean Durzi is out and missed their last game. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson.
Luke Glendening was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Taylor Raddysh and Eeli Tolvanen.
James Reimer was added to the roster on Oct 26.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

NYR.head: The Rangers have a slight edge
NYR.body: St. Louis has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Blues can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

STL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Blues

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers are on a four-game losing streak, while the Blues have won two in a row. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 20th).

The Blues have played better than their record (.536) says: their chances are worth about .593, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Rangers (.500 on chances worth .575), where their finishing has held them back.

The Blues keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st) and keep things calm after the whistle (lowest), but have struggled on the power play (32nd). On the other side, the Rangers forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), get their shots from in close (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Blues’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Rangers. Beyond that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Dylan Holloway (3 G / 9 A / 12 P in 14 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Joel Hofer (6-3-1 / .917 SV% in 10 GS) has been terrific for St. Louis and is expected to start. Dylan Garand (4-6-1 / .897 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for the Rangers.

items.text: The Blues are newly without Colton Parayko, and have had to make do without Logan Mailloux all season.
The Rangers are newly without Sean Durzi, and have been without Matthew Robertson for several games.
Jimmy Snuggerud has seven goals on chances worth about 3.0 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
